The dictionary store holds no record file for this source and the lane's source cache holds no copy of it, so the source audit (builder/write-fragments.mjs, evidence about the source and no part of any test) read the routes' own def field: on 40 of 40 routes the def is the pointed headword, a space, the route text and the citation of the index in square brackets with its page and entry number (axis: routes). The source's own key to its signs: none on file (the index's own front matter is not in the cache). The two pipes are the lane's own join, named in the Samaritan toggle strand's build rule (<tabernacle>/corpus-lane-builds/moses-samaritan-toggle-v1.4/build/RULE-build.md: lines " || " of Florentin–Tal and Wiktionary) and so verified from the lane's own file; every other shape's meaning begins "unverified:".

definitions.terms: In every test a character is one UTF-16 unit of the JavaScript string (every route here holds only characters of 16 bits). The text is the whole route text as it stands, the field route of a line of the by-source JSONL, what the checker gives the classifier, and never the field def. Nothing is trimmed unless a test says so. The text before the mark is every character from the start of the text up to, and not including, the mark; the text after the mark is every character after it to the end. The character before the mark is the one at the mark's index less one (none at the start of the text), the character after it the one at the mark's index plus one (none at the end). A letter is any character the JavaScript test \p{L} with the u flag matches; a digit is one of 0 to 9; a space character is U+0020 only; whitespace is what the JavaScript test \s matches; a Hebrew letter is a character from U+05D0 to U+05EA. The word before the mark is the longest run of letters that ends directly before the mark (empty if the character before it is not a letter). What the bracket holds means, for a bracket character, the characters between that opener and its closer: the template's c.group. Begins with the string means the string's characters are exactly the first characters, with nothing before them; with its leading whitespace taken off means the JavaScript trimStart. Is one of the strings in a list means is equal to one string of that list, character for character and whole. Every string and every list minds case. A string stands between « and », which are not part of it. Inside round brackets means the template's container paren; at top level means the container top.
definitions.first_match: For each mark the shapes are tried in the order they stand in this file; the first whose test holds names the occurrence, and no later shape is tried for it. Where a test says not caught above, it means the shapes listed above it for the same mark.

homonyms.reason: The route text carries no entry number; the index's entry number and page stand in the def field's citation, which the route drops, and 0 letters keys carry more than one text (axis: keys): each headword is one row, and the index's differences in meaning stand inside the row, joined by the lane's two pipes, so the count of keys with more than one text does not count them.

branches.question: A row of this index gives, for one headword, one meaning, or two or three meanings the Samaritan reading tells apart, with two pipes between each meaning and the next: Gen. 5.30, etc. || MT: 'fine linen'; SP: šeš. A row of one meaning has no pipes and is not in this question. Each side has its own three cells, the gloss, the Samaritan form and the places. Today the page prints the whole row as one pill. Does the pair of pipes divide, so that each meaning is a reading of its own? A cut at both pipes would leave an empty piece, so the cut would be at the first pipe, and the second would stay at the head of the next piece for the page to leave off.

options.means: The pipes do not cut: the page prints the whole row, every meaning with its cells, as one reading, as written, as it does today.

The first pipe of each pair cuts: the page prints the part up to Gen. 5.30, etc. and the part from MT: 'fine linen' on as two readings, each with its labels and its places. The second pipe of the pair stays at the head of the second piece as a lead sign, which the page leaves off the pill.

branches.question: Inside the quoted gloss of some rows two English wordings of one meaning stand with a comma between them: MT: 'desire, passion'; SP: tåwwå. Today the page prints the row whole. Does that comma divide, so that desire and passion are two readings, each inside its own part of the row? The quotation marks and the labels stay where they are, since the store's text does not change.

options.means: The comma does not cut: the page prints the row with 'desire, passion' whole, as written, as it does today.

The comma cuts: the page prints the part of the row up to desire and the part from passion on as two readings, each a run of the row's own characters, with the quotation mark of the gloss left on the side it stands.

not_done_here: This ledger leaves to the page the leaving off of the second pipe of a pair under B01's divides (the shape's lead sign), and the printing of the quoted gloss alone, which no kind of ask v1.2 can do since the gloss stands between two apostrophes and not in a bracket; it leaves to the store the 0 routes with no mark (axis: routes). Nothing is struck and no route is divided at rest.
